name: Rjili
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Blench 2020 Plateau survey/wordlist material cited on Glottolog; no phonology or grammar describing stress located

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Fittokka Gobak, Benard Abraham, Christina Riepe & Longdi Sylvanus. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Rjili (Tanjijili) [uji] Language of Niger State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-009. Dallas: SIL International. 55 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 9.3 'Phonetic inventories' (pp.19-22) gives consonant and vowel charts only ('initial cursory observations.. tentative'); Appendix E (p.37): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Tone is mentioned only incidentally (ethnonym variants differing in final-syllable tone); no word on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014 [draft first circulated 2006]. The Jijili (Koro) language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge (printout 12 March 2014). 27 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology is 'based on rapid observations'; 3.1 vowels, 3.2 consonants; 3.3 'Tones' is an empty heading (p.6); Introduction: 'In general, tones are not marked'. No mention of stress/accent.

sources.citation: Adebayo, Funke Christiana. 2011. Aspects of question formation in Ija-Koro. B.A. long essay, University of Ilorin (07/15CB012).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Same variety as Yusuf 2011 (identity uncertain); sec. 2.3 'Tonal system of Ija-Koro' (three tones); generic mention of suprasegmentals only; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Yusuf, Stephen Kunle. 2011. Aspects of Ija-Koro phonology. B.A. long essay, Dept. of Linguistics and Nigerian Languages, University of Ilorin (07/15CB107).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identity uncertain (labelled 'Ija-Koro', Bwari district; lexicon only partly Jilic-like and does not match the Rjili lists for head/two/three). Sec. 2.2 gives only a generic textbook list of suprasegmentals ('tones, intonation, stress, length'); ch. 4 describes a tone language with three register tones H, M, L and syllable types N, CV, V. No statement about word stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. Taped 1999 Adunnu Jijili wordlist / any tone-marked revision of 'The Jijili (Koro) language of Central Nigeria and its affinities' (he states tones 'will be added when time permits').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only primary linguist's data on Rjili; a tone-marked revision would be the first place any prosodic statement (tone vs. accent) could appear. No evidence such a revision exists.

sources.citation: Stoffberg, Yvonne. 1978b. Migili phonology. Language Data microfiche, African Series 14. Dallas: Summer Institute of Linguistics.

sources.note: Full phonology of the closest relative (Migili/Lijili [mgi], Jilic); would show whether the Jilic group is described with stress/accent in addition to tone. Not a description of Rjili itself (different glottocode, liji1238).
